key_insight: A BDF2-type finite element scheme for inertial magnetization dynamics is unconditionally stable and converges to a weak solution.
engineering_relevance: The method supports reliable simulation of subpicosecond magnetization dynamics relevant to ultrafast magnetic devices.
method: First-order finite elements in space and BDF2 time stepping.
Inertial term discretized using a convex combination of BDF2 and backward Euler.
Proves well-posedness, a discrete dissipative energy law, and explicit unit-length constraint error bounds.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments assess scheme performance and validate theoretical findings, but the abstract provides no quantitative results.
watch_item: Unconditional stability and convergence do not remove time-resolution requirements for accurately capturing ultrafast dynamics.
paper_title: An unconditionally convergent BDF2-type finite element integrator for the inertial Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation
